<reason>Side A won by establishing that direct revenue sharing creates a commercial labor relationship requiring durable antitrust immunity that only collective bargaining can provide, while effectively rebutting tax and Title IX concerns. Side B mounted a strong defense of the status quo, but Side A's rebuttals were sharper—particularly in exposing Side B's reliance on hypothetical congressional intervention as a concession that unilateral compliance is legally untenable, and in reframing workers' compensation objections as opposition to basic athlete protections.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>Side A's second rebuttal (A4), which directly answered the antitrust immunity pressure question for public universities with sophisticated non-statutory labor exemption and state-action immunity doctrine, while reframing Side B's workers' compensation complaint as a bizarre opposition to injury coverage for revenue-generating athletes.</best_rebuttal>
